title: Sum and intersection identity for Tate residues
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $C$ a commutative $k$-algebra, and $V$ a $C$-module. Let $A,B\subseteq V$ be $k$-subspaces such that $(fA+A)/A$ and $(fB+B)/B$ are finite-dimensional over $k$ for every $f\in C$. Then $A+B$ and $A\cap B$ have the same admissibility property. For the $k$-linear abstract residues $\operatorname{res}_{V,L}:\Omega^1_{C/k}\to k$ of [lem-pc-tate-abstract-residue-calculus], one has
$$\operatorname{res}_{V,A}+\operatorname{res}_{V,B}=\operatorname{res}_{V,A+B}+\operatorname{res}_{V,A\cap B}.$$

source.place: §2, property R5 and its proof, p. 153 (the sum/intersection property, numbered R3 in the upstream Lean module).

proof.text: Put $S=A+B$ and $I=A\cap B$. For subspaces write $X\prec Y$ when $(X+Y)/Y$ is finite-dimensional; equivalently $X\subseteq Y+E$ for some finite-dimensional $E$, by lifting a finite basis of the quotient. For fixed $f\in C$, choose finite-dimensional $E_A,E_B$ with $fA\subset A+E_A$ and $fB\subset B+E_B$. Then $fS\subset S+E_A+E_B$, so $S$ is admissible in the sense of [lem-pc-tate-abstract-residue-calculus]. The map $V/I\to V/A\oplus V/B$, $v+I\mapsto(v+A,v+B)$, is injective. Under it the image of $fI$ lies in the direct sum of the finite-dimensional images of $fA$ in $V/A$ and $fB$ in $V/B$. Thus $(fI+I)/I$ is finite-dimensional. This proves admissibility of $I$ for every $f$.

source.place: §2, property R5 and proof, printed p. 153; §1, T4 and its proof, printed p. 150.

proof.text: Choose complements $A=I\oplus A_0$, $B=I\oplus B_0$, and $V=I\oplus A_0\oplus B_0\oplus D$: extend a basis of $I$ to bases of $A,B$, and extend their union to one of $V$. Let $\pi_I,\pi_A,\pi_B,\pi_S$ be the coordinate projections onto $I$, $I\oplus A_0$, $I\oplus B_0$, and $I\oplus A_0\oplus B_0$. Checking the four summands gives $\pi_A+\pi_B=\pi_S+\pi_I$. All are $k$-linear projections onto their indicated subspaces.

source.place: §2, property R5 and proof, printed p. 153; §1, T4 and its proof, printed p. 150.

proof.text:
Fix $f,g\in C$ and, for $L\in\{I,A,B,S\}$, put $Z_L=\pi_Lm_{fg}-m_g\pi_Lm_f=[\pi_Lm_f,m_g]$. By [lem-pc-tate-abstract-residue-calculus], $\operatorname{res}_{V,L}(f\,dg)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(Z_L)$. We record explicit image bounds. Since $\pi_L(V)\subset L$, one has $Z_L(V)\subset L+gL\prec L$. Also $(\pi_L-1)m_f(L)$ and $(\pi_L-1)m_{fg}(L)$ are finite-dimensional: $fL\prec L$ and $fgL\prec L$, and $\pi_L-1$ kills $L$. On $L$ the identity
$$Z_L=(\pi_L-1)m_{fg}-m_g(\pi_L-1)m_f$$
therefore shows that $Z_L(L)$ is finite-dimensional. Multiplication by $g$ preserves finite-dimensionality, and $m_{fg}=m_gm_f$ because $C$ is commutative.

source.place: §2, property R5 and proof, printed p. 153; §1, T4 and its proof, printed p. 150.

proof.text: For $T\in\{Z_A,Z_S\}$, Step 3 gives $T(V)\prec S$, $T(S)\prec A$, and $T(A)\prec0$: for $Z_A$ use $Z_A(V)\prec A$ and its finite-dimensional restriction to $A$; for $Z_S$ use its finite-dimensional restriction to $S$. Every product $T_1T_2T_3$ of three of these operators has finite-dimensional image. Indeed $T_3(V)\subset S+E_3$ implies $T_2T_3(V)\subset A+E_2+T_2(E_3)$ and then $T_1T_2T_3(V)\subset E_1+T_1(E_2)+T_1T_2(E_3)$, for suitable finite-dimensional $E_i$. Define $W_{A,S}$ as the sum of the images of the eight products of length three. It is finite-dimensional and invariant under both operators: $T(T_1T_2T_3v)=(TT_1T_2)(T_3v)$ lies in one of those images. By expanding the cube, every $(cZ_A+dZ_S)^3(V)$ lies in $W_{A,S}$, for all $c,d\in k$.

source.place: §2, property R5 and proof, printed p. 153; §1, T4 and its proof, printed p. 150.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pc-finite-potent-trace-calculus] to the finite invariant subspace $W_{A,S}$ from Step 4, with $N=3$. For $T=Z_A,Z_S,Z_A-Z_S$ it identifies $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(T)$ with the ordinary trace of $T|_{W_{A,S}}$. The latter is the sum of its diagonal matrix entries [def-weil-endomorphism-trace], so subtraction of matrices gives
$$\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(Z_A)-\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(Z_S)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(Z_A-Z_S).$$
This uses one finite invariant subspace for all three operators; it does not assume additivity of Tate trace on arbitrary finite-potent operators.

source.place: §2, property R5 and proof, printed p. 153; §1, T4 and its proof, printed p. 150.

proof.text:
For the second pair $T\in\{Z_I,Z_B\}$, Step 3 gives $T(V)\prec B$, $T(B)\prec I$, and $T(I)\prec0$. For $Z_I$ its full image is almost in $I$ and its restriction to $I$ is finite-dimensional; for $Z_B$ its restriction to $B$ is finite-dimensional, hence so is its restriction to $I\subset B$. Explicitly the same three containments as Step 4, with $S,A$ replaced by $B,I$, show that all eight products of length three have finite-dimensional image. Their sum $W_{I,B}$ is invariant under both operators, since $T(T_1T_2T_3v)=(TT_1T_2)(T_3v)$; the cubes of $Z_I$, $Z_B$, and $Z_I-Z_B$ have image in it. The restriction characterization of [lem-pc-finite-potent-trace-calculus] and the diagonal-entry definition of [def-weil-endomorphism-trace] therefore give
$$\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(Z_I)-\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(Z_B)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(Z_I-Z_B).$$

source.place: §2, property R5 and proof, printed p. 153; §1, T4 and its proof, printed p. 150.

proof.text:
The projection identity of Step 2 implies the exact operator identity
$$Z_A-Z_S=[(\pi_A-\pi_S)m_f,m_g]=[(\pi_I-\pi_B)m_f,m_g]=Z_I-Z_B.$$
Steps 5 and 6 consequently give $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(Z_A)-\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(Z_S)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(Z_I)-\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(Z_B)$. Substituting the residue formulas of [lem-pc-tate-abstract-residue-calculus] from Step 3 and rearranging in $k$ proves
$$\operatorname{res}_{V,A}(f\,dg)+\operatorname{res}_{V,B}(f\,dg)=\operatorname{res}_{V,S}(f\,dg)+\operatorname{res}_{V,I}(f\,dg).$$

source.place: §2, property R5 and proof, printed p. 153; §1, T4 and its proof, printed p. 150.

proof.text: By the generators-and-relations construction in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], $\Omega^1_{C/k}$ is generated as a $C$-module by the symbols $dg$, hence as a $k$-vector space by $f\,dg$ with $f,g\in C$. Each residue is $k$-linear by [lem-pc-tate-abstract-residue-calculus]. The identity of Step 7 on these generators therefore extends to every differential, proving the asserted equality of $k$-linear maps.

source.place: §2, property R5 and proof, printed p. 153; §1, T4 and its proof, printed p. 150.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q106-7b973cb2e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, all 4 cited statements (lem-pc-tate-abstract-residue-calculus, lem-pc-finite-potent-trace-calculus, def-weil-endomorphism-trace, def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials), the citer lem-pc-tate-adelic-reciprocity, the unit sk-thm-picard-duality, and Tate ASENS 1968 §1 T1-T5 (pp.149-150), Thm 1 and Remark (*) (pp.151-152), and R5 with its proof (p.153). The statement is unchanged and agrees with R5 hypothesis by hypothesis, including both admissibility conclusions. Step 1: the sum is admissible because fS lies in S+E_A+E_B; the intersection is admissible through the injection V/I into V/A+V/B. Step 2: I checked that basis-of-I plus A_0 plus B_0 is independent, and that pi_A+pi_B=pi_S+pi_I on each of the four summands. Step 3: Z_L=[pi_L m_f,m_g] is exactly the residue node's formula; I verified the expansion Z_L=(pi_L-1)m_fg - m_g(pi_L-1)m_f, which gives finite Z_L(L). Steps 4 and 6: I checked the filtrations V>S>A>0 for Z_A,Z_S and V>B>I>0 for Z_I,Z_B; the eight length-3 words have finite image and span an invariant W containing every cube. This is Tate's 'finite potent subspace' and T4 proof written out. Step 5 uses only the trace-calculus sentence 'equals Tr_k(T|_U) for finite T-stable U containing T^N(V)' plus matrix additivity, not the pairwise-product clause, whose hypothesis does not hold here. Step 7: Z_A-Z_S=Z_I-Z_B exactly, as in Tate's display. Step 8: Omega^1 is k-spanned by f dg, and the residues are k-linear. Edge cases: A=B, A in B, A=0, B=V, V finite-dimensional, char 2, non-domain C, and the citer's disjoint-summand use. No new nodes, no duplicate (lem-pc-tate-endomorphism-ideals covers a single A), no cycle (the cited unsplit nodes have empty proof_deps), same-unit route, no SGA, no tool_uses, and proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. Maintainer note: TateResidue.res_sup_add_res_inf covers the equality clause only, as the report says. No fixes.
